name: Mozambique
sources: GDP $3.9bn: STATED SUBSTITUTION OF YEAR, and the substitution is forced. World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.CD, series MOZ, HAS NO 1990 ENTRY — the series begins in 1991, and it begins at 3,854,856,434. That 1991 print is what has been entered, rounded to 3.9. It is defensible in real terms because the World Bank's own real-growth series NY.GDP.MKTP.KD.ZG puts 1990 at +1.00% and 1991 at +4.93%, so 1990 output was a few points below 1991 output; what it cannot capture is the current-dollar path, because the metical was being devalued in steps under the Programa de Reabilitacao Economica and a current-dollar level is a statement about the exchange rate as much as about production.

A SECOND CAVEAT ON THE SAME NUMBER, stated rather than hidden, because it is the one a reader will trip over. Contemporary sources routinely call Mozambique the poorest country in the world in 1990 and put GNP per capita at about $80, from the World Bank Atlas of the period converting at the official rate. $3.9bn over 13.1m people is $298 a head, nearly four times that. The gap is the old Atlas conversion against the rebuilt national-accounts series, not a disagreement about how poor Mozambique was; NY.GDP.MKTP.CD is the series the whole roster sits on and consistency with it is why the larger figure is entered. Either way Mozambique opens as one of the two or three poorest states on the board.

Population 13.1m: World Bank SP.POP.TOTL, series MOZ, 1990 = 13,094,537. This counts the people inside the borders and therefore understates the dislocation: roughly 1.5m Mozambicans were refugees in Malawi, Zimbabwe, South Africa, Tanzania, Zambia and Swaziland by 1990 and perhaps 3m more were displaced inside the country. Malawi alone was holding close to 900,000 of them, about a tenth of its own population.

TFP trend 0.004: set level with Kenya's and BELOW Tanzania's 0.005, and the reason is the war rather than the policy. The policy was the same as Tanzania's and started a year later — the PRE of January 1987, IMF-agreed, which devalued the metical, freed most prices and returned trade to private hands, and produced real growth of 8.2% in 1988 and 6.5% in 1989 off a floor. What Tanzania did not have is an insurgency whose stated method was the destruction of the capital stock: RENAMO had wrecked on the order of 1,800 primary schools and a large share of rural health posts by 1990, and the Beira and Limpopo corridors ran only because foreign troops stood on them. Productivity growth net of that is Kenya's number, not Tanzania's.

Inflation 47%: NOT FROM THE WORLD BANK SERIES and flagged. FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG has no Mozambican entry for 1990 and the GDP deflator NY.GDP.DEFL.KD.ZG has none before 1992 (which prints 37.8). 47% is the figure carried in the IMF's Recent Economic Developments reporting for calendar 1990, against an all-time high near 61% in 1991; it is entered as the best available and listed as an admitted gap. The direction is not in doubt — the PRE was a sequence of devaluations, and prices under it went up.

Interest rate 42%: NOT SOURCED IN THIS SESSION. FR.INR.LEND has no Mozambican entry for 1990 or for any nearby year. 0.42 is entered as a bracket for a Banco de Mocambique rate that the PRE had been raising since 1987 and that was still short of inflation, which was the point of it: negative real rates were what the pre-1987 regime ran on and the programme was walking them back rather than closing them at a stroke. The loader's coupled real-rate check reads 0.025 - (0.42 - 0.47) = 0.075 — negative in real terms, so the sign is preserved, and only mildly so. BOTH FIGURES IN THIS PAIR ARE BRACKETS, and where both sides of a pair are brackets the pair should be set near neutral rather than wide: the demand channel in economy.rs is linear in the distance from neutral at 0.55 to annual growth, so an unsourced guess at the rate is also a guess at Mozambique's growth. An earlier draft of this file entered 0.35, which is a gap of 0.145 and opens a country that actually grew 1.00% in 1990 at about +8% a year. The reasoning is set out at length in zambia.json, where the same problem arrives with one side sourced and is much worse.

Revenue 14% of GDP: NOT SOURCED — GC.REV.XGRT.GD.ZS has no Mozambican entry — and entered as a bracket a point above Tanzania's 13% and two above Ethiopia's 12%. Flagged. The number that matters and that this field cannot hold is the other one: Mozambique in 1990 was running on foreign aid at a scale almost no other state has ever run on, of the order of half of national income, and the state's own take was a minor part of what it spent.

Military 2.4% of GDP: World Bank MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS, series MOZ, 1990 = 2.39, down from 3.37 in 1989. SURPRISINGLY LOW for a country in the fourteenth year of a civil war, and it is entered as printed rather than adjusted upward to fit the story. Two things explain it without contradicting it: much of what the FPLM fielded was Soviet-supplied rather than bought, and the two corridors were being defended by Zimbabwean and Tanzanian troops on somebody else's budget.

Investment 30% of GDP, split 21 state / 9 private: the total is the 1991 print of gross capital formation (World Bank NE.GDI.TOTL.ZS, series MOZ, 1991 = 31.60; no 1990 entry exists) rounded down, and THE SPLIT IS APPORTIONED, not transcribed. It is weighted hard toward the state because nearly all of it was donor-financed public reconstruction — ports, rail, the Cahora Bassa line — and private fixed investment in a country where an insurgency was burning plant was close to nothing.

Debt 125% of GDP: World Bank DT.DOD.DECT.GN.ZS, series MOZ, 1991 = 124.62, external debt stocks as a share of GNI. STATED SUBSTITUTION OF YEAR — the series has no 1990 entry — and the figure is rising fast on both sides of it: 190.9% by 1992 and 255.6% by 1994. Mozambique reached HIPC completion in 2001.

Oil 0.0: no production. The Pande and Temane gas fields were known but undeveloped; the energy asset that mattered was Cahora Bassa, whose transmission lines to South Africa RENAMO had cut and kept cut since 1981.

Stability 24 and authoritarianism 0.75: stability is set between Ethiopia's 22 and Angola's 26, which is the right company and the right order. FRELIMO held the cities, the corridors and the coast and did not hold much else; the war had killed on the order of several hundred thousand people by 1990, mostly civilians and mostly of hunger, and would kill more before the Rome accords of 4 October 1992. Authoritarianism 0.75 is a sole legal party with a state security service (SNASP), set above Tanzania's 0.72 and below Ethiopia's, and it is a number in motion: FRELIMO dropped Marxism-Leninism at its fifth congress in July 1989 and the constitution of 2 November 1990 legalised opposition parties, ten months after the game starts.

Separatism 0.03: LOW ON PURPOSE, and it is the most likely thing in this file to be read as an error. Mozambique in 1990 had a civil war and almost no secessionism. RENAMO wanted Maputo, not a partition — it was built by Rhodesian and then South African intelligence as an instrument against FRELIMO and it ran on rural grievance and coercion rather than on a nation wanting out. There is no Mozambican Eritrea and there is no Mozambican Cabinda, which is exactly why the number is a fifth of Angola's 0.30 while stability is lower than Angola's. The model should read this as a state losing control of its territory, not as a state coming apart into pieces.

Military strength 3: the Forcas Populares de Libertacao de Mocambique were nominally 60,000-70,000, Soviet-equipped, conscripted and unable to hold ground away from the garrisons — which is why Zimbabwe kept roughly 10,000 troops on the Beira corridor and Tanzania several thousand more in the north. Set level with Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda at 3 on size and below Zimbabwe's 5 on everything else. A large army that cannot secure its own country is exactly what this index is meant to be able to say.

pop_growth_1990 = 0.9416%/yr. Compound annual growth of World Bank SP.POP.TOTL, series MOZ (Mozambique): 12,315,954 in 1984 to 12,906,842 in 1989 — the five years ending on the eve of the 1 January 1990 start date. See EconomyRecord::pop_growth_1990 in spheres-sim/src/data/mod.rs for why the window ends in 1989 and not with the single-year 1990 rate.

reserves_bn = 0.203 ($bn). Total reserves including gold, MOZ, 1989: US$203495525.25 (World Bank World Development Indicators series FI.RES.TOTL.CD, 'Total reserves (includes gold, current US$)', retrieved from the World Bank API on 2026-09-02; indicator lastupdated 2026-07-13). THE 1989 OBSERVATION AND NOT THE 1990 ONE: a reserve is a stock, and the stock on the morning of the 1 January 1990 start date is the end-1989 figure - the same reasoning pop_growth_1990 above gives for ending its window on 31 December 1989. LIMIT STATED: this series is official reserve assets. Sovereign wealth fund balances are not in it and none has been added, because no audited 1990 balance could be sourced for any of them; where that materially understates a state's usable stock it is reported rather than estimated (iron rule 4).

note: 1990 TECHNOLOGY: AUTHORED, NOT DERIVED. What this nation knew on 1 January 1990 is transcribed and sourced grant by grant, exactly like every other 1990 figure in this file, and is not read off tfp_trend - there was never a code path from the trend to the known set, and the zero that stood there was a claim about the world rather than an absence of one (BIBLE section 8 and iron rule 4, both amended 2026-08-30). THE PREDICATE IS SPLIT, and split by the technology's OWN EFFECT TYPE so that it is mechanically computable and never a per-nation judgement call. A node whose effects include MilitaryEfficiency, MilitaryStrength, DiffusionEmission or CostReduction is SOVEREIGNTY-SIDE: holding it means this nation could PRODUCE it, so operating an imported article does not qualify. Every other node is USE-SIDE: deployed and in operational use here is enough, whoever built it, because the effect such a node pays is a productivity, health or output effect and that effect is real in the country where the machine runs. Of the 48 technologies the tree lets anyone hold in 1990, 17 are sovereignty-side and 31 are use-side.

DATA-KEYED TAIL NATION. This nation is outside the 29 authored majors, so nothing here was authored technology by technology: a grant is made only where one of two named published global series supports it, and nothing is modelled, estimated or interpolated. A short list, or an empty one, is the correct outcome of that rule and not a gap in the work.

Data-keyed tail nation: not one of the 29 authored majors. Only the two series named in ruling 3 were consulted - WHO/UNICEF WUENIC DTP3 1990 and World Bank IT.CEL.SETS. Nothing was modelled, estimated or interpolated, and no other evidence was admitted. ISO3 key used for both series: MOZ.
AUTHORED, AND THE ANSWER IS NOTHING. Both named series were checked and both refused this nation; the empty grant list is a finding, not an absence of work.
WUENIC DTP3 1990 = 46% against the 80% UCI-1990 threshold: refused.
IT.CEL.SETS at 31 December 1989 = 0 against a threshold of any positive count: refused.

The other 46 grantable 1990 technologies are BLANK for this nation by design, not by oversight: the 17 sovereignty-side entries are unreachable by any use-in-operation series, and no published global series was named that keys the remaining 29 use-side entries.
